A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLIP experiments on typographic robustness, gender classification and retrieval, knowledge retention, and CIFAR-10 adversarial robustness, including quantitative results and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their numerical and qualitative outcomes, including the benchmark tables, gender-control demonstrations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The DPO/IPO/KTO adaptation, KL regularization, singular-value control, and BMA procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. The added overview and figure explanations do not modify the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic and real-world typographic datasets, ImageNetV2 evaluation, FOOD101/SUN analyses, VL-Bias gender tasks, and CIFAR-10 PGD experiments. Moving Table 2 to Appendix F and adding an ImageNetV2 citation do not change coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain CLIP, Materzynska+, PAINT, and Defense-Prefix. The cross-entropy and EMA comparisons also remain. Materzynska is explicitly included in v3's baseline enumeration but was already evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: No previously stated metric, training budget, hyperparameter, attack strength, or evaluation procedure changes. Appendix K newly identifies existing plots as training curves and Table 7 as validation results; this is additional documentation, not evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The saliency and VQGAN examples, orthogonality checks, hyperparameter sweeps, BMA/EMA comparison, sample-efficiency analyses, and PGD tests are retained. Splitting v2 Figure 6 into v3 Figures 6–7 redisplays the same diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 0 and retain the same distribution plots. Neither introduces additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or revised uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The tables and matched plots retain their results. For example, Table 1's KTO averages remain 57.09% clean and 51.74% typographic, and Table 2's IPO average remains 67.54%. The new 19.63-point statement in Section 4.1 restates the existing EuroSAT difference.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, policy-ratio and gradient results, regularization arguments, SVD construction, and Appendix B proofs remain mathematically unchanged. The orthogonality and BMA derivations are also retained; equation punctuation and reference formatting are editorial changes.

C1.justification: Both versions claim preference optimization for contrastive models, concept control through singular values, and improved robustness and gender-bias mitigation while preserving pretrained knowledge. The shortened abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of knowledge retention, OCR/object trade-offs, gender control, sample efficiency, and hyperparameter sensitivity are unchanged. The expanded Appendix C prose repeats explanations previously contained in v2 Figure 6's caption; no substantive limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix K explicitly distinguishes training accuracies in v3 Figures 16–17 from validation-set results in Table 7, whereas v2 presents the same evidence without that distinction. Hardware, optimization settings, pseudocode, and the code-access link otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Recht et al. (2019) for the already-used ImageNetV2 dataset. The IPO reference changes from its preprint to its published version, and KTO citation formatting is corrected; these are not new works or substantive changes in research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 tightens the abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion, adds a short method overview, and refines appendix headings and subsections. It also updates affiliations and publication headers and adds acknowledgments. Most technical prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 1 moves to the method opening, Table 2 moves to Appendix F, and v2 Figure 6 becomes two separately labeled figures. Several other figures receive separate panel captions, resized panels, or revised labels, including the t* annotation in Figure 3. These changes largely redisplay existing evidence.

improvement.justification: Moving the method overview earlier, separating the crowded diagnostic panels, and clarifying training versus validation results make v3 easier to follow and assess. Table 2 becomes less prominent in the appendix but remains available. The methods, proofs, and empirical support are unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to clearer presentation and documentation.
